output.summary: An annual flowering plant native to the southern United States and northern Mexico, smallflower desert-chicory grows in prairies, clay soils and disturbed places. Its flowers open in the morning, broken stems release milky sap, and its dried seeds resemble dandelion puffs. The roots are brewed as tea or coffee, while the bitter edible leaves are often boiled.
output.edibilityNote: Roots are brewed as tea or coffee; bitter leaves are often boiled, and the plant can also be made into jelly.
